metadata.title: Does Claude's Digest Skill Watch You All Week?
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude's digest skill works because Claude has been continuously aware of everything across your connected sources -- or something narrower. Lands the carry-out that digest is a file that runs when you ask, and unless you say 'weekly', it hands you one day and calls it done.
metadata.source_note: Source sheet's narration carries real skill-specific facts (not unfilled template placeholders) -- see QUESTION.md. Facts preserved: digest generates a daily or weekly digest of activity across all connected sources -- used when catching up after time away, starting the day, or reviewing a week's decisions and document updates grouped by project; the design tell (default to --daily if no flag is specified) is preserved and turned into the falsifying case. Register re-registered Teardown -> Plain; source's B03/BVDT design-tell verdict became a plain mechanism + both-directions beat; a wrong-guess beat and an anchor (Monday, week away, unnamed window: asked -> reads file -> steps run -> returned 'Friday only') were added per hai-simple's Phase 1 structure, since the source's Teardown shape carried neither.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 (Monday, week away, unnamed window: asked -> reads file -> steps run -> returned 'Friday only', then paid off into 'still unset -- same one-day default' / 'say weekly -- all seven days')

beats.narration_text: Someone wonders whether Claude was quietly watching everything while they were away. It wasn't. Liam is here to take you through what the digest skill actually does, step by step.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'All week I was away -- was Claude quietly watching?', hesitates on 'watching', corrects to 'waiting', lands the real question

props.text:
All week I was away —
was Claude quietly
watching?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('watching' -> 'waiting') is visible on a late frame, fully settled before the beat ends.

beats.narration_text: The natural guess is that Claude has been quietly aware of everything happening across your sources, so asking for a digest just taps into something it already knows. But nothing runs until you ask — and even then, if you don't say how far back to look, it defaults to just one day. Come back from a week away, ask for a digest without saying "weekly," and what surfaces is Friday. Six days of decisions and mentions never make it in.

shot.new_visual_element: An 'AWARE ALL WEEK' figure with a scattered eye-mark cluster, struck through; an 'ASK -> DEFAULT DAILY' card lit instead

production_viz.label: Always aware, struck -- ask, then default daily, lit
production_viz.mechanic: Left: a figure icon labelled 'AWARE ALL WEEK' beside a scattered cluster of small eye-marks. Right: a card labelled 'ASK -> DEFAULT DAILY' listing the steps: reads file, checks for a flag, defaults to one day if none given. The aware side dims and gets a terracotta strike; the ask/default card stays lit. A final line sits outside the card: 'week away, no flag -- Friday only'.

beats.narration_text: What the skill actually does: read one instruction file, then follow its steps in order — gather mentions and action items across your connected sources, group updates by project, and check whether you asked for daily or weekly. Watch the anchor: it's Monday, you've been gone all week, and you ask for a digest without naming a window. The file's default line fires — daily, unless told otherwise — and what comes back covers one day: yesterday's mentions, yesterday's decisions. The other six days sit outside it.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- a 'Monday, week away' question traveling asked -> reads file -> steps run -> returned, landing on a seven-box week strip with one box lit

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- one Monday, four stops, one day back
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Four stacked cards labelled 'ASKED', 'READS FILE', 'STEPS RUN', 'RETURNED'. A single highlighted token 'MONDAY, WEEK AWAY' travels down through all four cards in turn, each lighting terracotta as it arrives. Beside the RETURNED card, a row of seven small boxes (a week strip) appears: only the last box (Friday) lights terracotta, the other six stay ink-dim. A small note reads 'one day back'. THIS EXACT WEEK-STRIP COMPOSITION RETURNS, CONDENSED, AT B03.

beats.narration_text: That one day is what the file returns every time the window is left unset — ask again tomorrow without saying weekly, and you get today, identically, every time. But say weekly once, and the same file runs the same steps across all seven days instead, surfacing everything the daily default left out. Same file, same steps — what changes is only the word you remembered to say.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS, condensed; splits into two week strips -- one box lit ('still unset') and all seven lit ('said weekly')

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- still unset, or said weekly
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 COMPOSITION RETURNS, condensed to a small resting row (READS FILE / STEPS RUN / RETURNED). It shrinks and slides up. Two week-strips fade in beneath: left strip has only its last box lit terracotta, labelled 'STILL UNSET' then 'SAME DEFAULT' with a checkmark (holds); right strip has all seven boxes lit terracotta, labelled 'SAID WEEKLY' then a struck-through 'ONE DAY?' (flips).

beats.narration_text: A Claude digest isn't Claude quietly watching all week — it's a file that runs when you ask, and unless you say weekly, it hands you one day and calls it done.

props.sparkLine: Runs when asked. Covers what you name.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Run the digest skill on your own connected sources without saying whether you want daily or weekly, and see which window it defaults to. Then run it again, this time saying weekly explicitly, and compare what surfaces that the first pass missed. Liam, in for Bear.
